title: Mask Adoption Simulation
description: Simulate the adoption and compliance dynamics of mask-wearing in a population influenced by peer effects, policies, messaging, and supply constraints.

interactions.name: peer_influence
interactions.description: People observe mask use among their social neighbors and update adoption based on thresholds and influence strength.

interactions.name: policy_enforcement
interactions.description: Locations with mask policies enforce compliance; people decide whether to comply based on enforcement and personal propensity.

interactions.name: information_diffusion
interactions.description: Authorities and media channels disseminate messages that update individuals' trust, risk perception, and adoption propensity.

interactions.name: mobility_and_contacts
interactions.description: People move among locations and encounter others; observed compliance and contacts affect perceived norms and costs.

interactions.name: supply_acquisition
interactions.description: People attempt to acquire masks subject to supply levels and costs, which impacts their ability to adopt or sustain masking.

metrics.name: adoption_rate_over_time
metrics.description: Proportion of people wearing masks at each time step.

metrics.name: final_adoption_rate
metrics.description: Adoption rate at the end of the simulation period.

metrics.name: peak_adoption_rate
metrics.description: Maximum adoption rate achieved during the simulation and the day it occurs.

metrics.name: time_to_50_percent_adoption
metrics.description: Number of days until adoption rate first reaches or exceeds 50%.

metrics.name: compliance_rate_under_mandate
metrics.description: Average proportion of people complying with mask mandates at locations where mandates apply.

metrics.name: violation_rate
metrics.description: Rate at which individuals enter mandated locations without masking.

metrics.name: adoption_by_location_type
metrics.description: Average observed mask use within each location type.

metrics.name: campaign_effect_lift
metrics.description: Difference in adoption rate attributable to messaging campaigns versus a no-campaign baseline.
